paper.citation: Xinkun Nie and Stefan Wager (2021). Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Biometrika, 108(2):299–319. DOI 10.1093/biomet/asaa076
paper.title: Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects
paper.source_version: Published typeset article deposited in NSF PAR, 21 PDF pages; issue year 2021; publisher first-online metadata 2020-09-24
paper.source_locator: Section 6.1, PDF p.15 / journal p.313, unnumbered shared sampling equations and Set-ups A–D; Section 6.2 / Figure 3, PDF p.16 / journal p.314 for dimension and noise settings; collected paragraph: Set-up D

mechanism.name: 不相关的正部函数处理与对照响应
mechanism.title_en: Three-term assignment and unrelated positive-part outcomes
generation_equations: Y=b(X)+(A-0.5)*tau(X)+epsilon, epsilon~N(0,1); equivalently E[Y|X,A=1]=u and E[Y|X,A=0]=v.

sampling.dependence: Five active covariates; disjoint nonlinear conditional means and treatment interactions. The three-term propensity denominator is retained; it is not expit(X1+X2). No uniform overlap bound is claimed. Independent treatment/noise random draws conditional on covariates; no clusters or panel structure.

assumptions: Consistency and no interference across independent individuals.
Conditional exchangeability given observed baseline X under the declared synthetic assignment.
Pointwise positivity; no uniform overlap bound claimed for unbounded Gaussian logistic settings.

properties.notes: Five active covariates; disjoint nonlinear conditional means and treatment interactions. The three-term propensity denominator is retained; it is not expit(X1+X2). No uniform overlap bound is claimed.

estimand.name: ATE
estimand.definition: E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the full declared covariate population; treatment 1 versus 0; population, not sample-conditional, target.

truth.expression: E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the full declared covariate population; treatment 1 versus 0; population, not sample-conditional, target.
truth.derivation: X1+X2+X3~N(0,3), X4+X5~N(0,2). For S~N(0,v), E[max(S,0)]=sqrt(v/(2*pi)). Thus ATE=(sqrt(3)-sqrt(2))/sqrt(2*pi).

adaptations: Target explicitly changed from conditional effect tau(x) to population ATE E[tau(X)]; original data-generating law retained. No claim that the source reports this ATE numerical value.
Source treatment indicator is named A in the observed output; no scientific change.
Independently implemented Python/NumPy sampler; source estimator fitting and large simulation replications are outside this collection task.
